text:
Letter dated April 14, 1972, from Deputy Commissioner, Kentucky Department of Natural Resources with appended comments from Assistant Commissioner, Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources and from the Kentucky Program Development Office.
Comment: The Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources suggests that State/Federal agreements for management and protection of endangered species be provided by more binding wording. Section 8(b) of HR 4758 reads, "The Secretary may enter into agreements with the States for the administration and management of any area established for the conservation, protection, restoration, and propagation of endangered species." The review draft of the EIS reads, "...the Secretary would be authorized to enter into agreements with the States for management and administration of programs of areas established for the conservation, restoration, protection, or propagation of endangered animals." Kentucky proposes that this reference be changed to, "The Secretary would be directed wherever and whenever possible to enter into agreements with the States..."
Response: If the Secretary is to be responsible for administration of the program, he must be authorized to enter into only those agreements which he deems in the best interest of the endangered species involved. Therefore the term "may" is used. The wording proposed by Kentucky includes the condition, "wherever and whenever possible" to denote Secretarial discretion. However, we believe the condition "may" is preferable.
<u>Comment</u>: Kentucky questions the exemption of American Indians, Aleuts and  Eskimos from the provisions of HR 1311 thereby allowing these groups to  take endangered species for their own use.
